explain.say: Imagine passing a note that only your best friend can read, even if someone else grabs it. That is what encryption does, which means scrambling a message so only the right person can read it. Look at the first box: our message is HELLO.

explain.say: Now look at the second box. We use a very old trick called a Caesar cipher: move every letter 3 places along the alphabet. H becomes K, E becomes H, L becomes O. Can you work out what O becomes?

explain.say: Yes, O becomes R! So HELLO turns into KHOOR. See the third box? That scrambled text is called ciphertext. If a snooper grabs it, they just see nonsense. What would you need to read it?

explain.say: You need the key! Here the key is the number 3. Your friend shifts each letter back 3 and gets HELLO again, which is called decrypting. But look at the board: a Caesar code is easy to crack. Why would only 25 tries be enough?

faq.a: Encryption scrambles a message using a key, so only someone with the right key can unscramble, or decrypt, it. Messaging apps, banks and secure websites all use it.
asks: How do apps keep messages private?

faq.a: A Caesar cipher shifts every letter a fixed number of places along the alphabet. With a shift of 3, A becomes D and HELLO becomes KHOOR. It is named after Julius Caesar.
asks: How does a Caesar cipher work?

faq.a: The key is the secret that locks and unlocks the message. In a Caesar cipher it is the shift number; in modern encryption it is a huge random number.
asks: What is a key in cryptography?

faq.q: Why is a Caesar cipher easy to crack?
faq.a: There are only 25 possible shifts, so you can try them all in minutes. Common letters like E also give it away.
asks: How do you break a Caesar cipher?

faq.a: It means a message is scrambled on your phone and only unscrambled on your friend's phone, so not even the app company in between can read it.

facts: The Roman historian Suetonius wrote that Julius Caesar encrypted letters by shifting each letter three places along the alphabet.
A 128-bit key has 2 to the power 128 possible values, about 3.4 × 10^38.

quiz.say: Using a Caesar shift of 3, what does the word CAT become?
quiz.show: CAT with a shift of 3 is…
quiz.why: C plus 3 is F, A plus 3 is D, T plus 3 is W: FDW.

wrong.1: That is a shift of 1, not 3.
wrong.2: That shifts backwards by 3 instead of forwards.

quiz.say: What do you need to unscramble an encrypted message?
quiz.show: To decrypt a message you need…
quiz.why: The key is the secret that reverses the scrambling.

wrong.1: Screen size does not unlock a code.
wrong.2: Speed does not help without the key.
